we offer a special prayer of .comfort for the loss of our loved ones god our father as we remember those who have gone before us this november give us the comfort of knowing that they have gone only as far as you and you are very near. amen. remembrance service our annual service of remembrance takes place in st. mary of the rosary on monday 2 november at 7pm. all welcome. calvary monument following a detailed proposal from within the parish community we have decided to relocate the calvary monument from its current location to a new site. this decision was reached following comprehensive evaluation and investigation by both the parish finance committee and the parish pastoral council. the new site is between the pathway to the castle garden and to the left of our lady’s statue (south-east from main entrance). the proposed work will take place in the coming weeks. the current location will be converted back to its previous use as a lawn space. the project will be funded by a private sponsor from within the parish community. our nearness to eternity it has been traditional in ireland to regard the dead as very close to us who are living. peig sayers, a traditional storyteller who lived on the great blasket island off the kerry coast was once asked where heaven was. in reply she said it was just a few inches above the head of the tallest man on the island. heaven and earth, like life and death were one in the traditional way of thinking. whether or not peig realized it, her belief about heaven’s closeness to earth is very similar to the thinking of the great medieval mystic known as meister eckhart. when he was asked where does the soul go after death eckhart said, ‘no place. where else would the soul be going, where else is the eternal world? it can be nowhere other than here.’ we have somehow managed to lose that sense of the nearness of eternity and to forget that once the soul is free of the body, time and space, distance and separation are meaningless.
